title: Cost Mosaic: Interactive Token Attribution Grid and Exportable Pricing Patterns
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Objective: Design an interactive, exportable token-level cost analysis view that helps product and finance teams reconcile per-route pricing with token consumption. The view ("Cost Mosaic") combines a pivotable grid, time-slice filters, and pricing pattern presets so users can both inspect and export normalized ledgers for downstream analytics.

Scope: Surface per-message and per-token breakdowns (model, route, user, prompt template), attribution shares (proportional or rule-based), and applied pricing pattern (slab, tier, custom per-customer). Include CSV & Parquet export templates, a lightweight preview of how pricing rules change totals, and UI patterns for showing uncertainty when rollups are estimated (e.g., cached tokens vs. recomputed).

Out of scope for this ticket: billing engine implementation, multi-org cost rollup, SSO entitlement gating. This ticket is focused on UX, prototype, and export schema definition so Eng can implement with a normalized ledger payload.
acceptance_criteria: Interactive grid where rows can be grouped by model, route, or customer and columns show raw tokens, effective unit price, and computed cost
Quick-preview pricing presets (Slab, Flat, Per-1k, Custom allocation) that apply immediately and update totals in the UI
Export option producing a normalized ledger (CSV + Parquet) with documented column schema and pricing metadata
Prototype validated in design review with PM, Billing SME, and 2 engineers and resulting feedback captured
Aria/accessibility checks for keyboard navigation and screenreader labels on the pivot controls
notes: 2025-01-31 AK: Kickoff with PM (Morgan Hale) and Billing SME (Priya Desai) — confirmed export must be BI-friendly (no nested payloads).
2025-02-03 LC: Low-fidelity sketches reviewed — feedback: allow rule preview without committing to export; include a 'difference' column when comparing pricing presets.
2025-02-07 AK: Design critique — accessibility and table performance concerns raised; decided to lazy-load row groups and provide client-side pagination.
2025-02-11 PD: Billing SME review — asked to include pricing metadata: applied_slabs, currency, effective_start/end, and reference_rate_id in export schema (added to attachments).

2025-02-15 LC: Built interactive Figma prototype; demoed to 6 PMs and 2 SREs. Outcome: strong alignment on grid affordances; request to expose raw token buckets (prompt, completion, cached) as optional columns.
2025-02-18 AK: Updated prototype and acceptance criteria; ready for handoff to frontend with export-schema PR referenced in attachments.
design_decisions: Use a pivotable grid (rows = grouping dimension, columns = metric buckets) rather than a free-form Sankey to make exports deterministic
Expose both per-token unit price (e.g., $/1k tokens) and computed total cost to prevent rounding confusion
Color encoding will be applied to attribution share column using a 3-step diverging palette to highlight high-cost consumers

Export schema v1 will be flat (one row per atomic message) with normalized columns: timestamp, customer_id, route, model_id, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, cached_tokens, unit_price_per_1k, applied_pricing_pattern, computed_cost, pricing_metadata_ref
Provide a 'pricing preview' mode that calculates estimated totals client-side using the same pricing engine inputs but flags rows marked as 'estimate' when full ledger reconciliation is required
next_steps: Finalize export column names and add to PRD (owner: Aisha)
Handoff high-fidelity components to frontend (owner: Liam) with tokenized CSS vars for color tokens
Sync with ENG-15842 on backend normalized ledger payload and sample dataset
Schedule billing validation session with Priya and finance on 2025-02-25
Write QA checklist for exports (consistency, currency, slippage between presets)
user_research_summary: Light-weight validation with 6 PMs and 2 SREs focused on two flows: (1) reconcile a 7-day spend window to identify top-3 cost drivers, (2) export a normalized ledger for downstream BI. Participants preferred a tabular, pivot-first approach and wanted explicit 'explain' affordances on how pricing presets change totals. Usability issues: initial discoverability of pricing presets and confusion around cached vs recomputed tokens; addressed in prototype with inline tooltips and a collapsed 'token breakdown' column.
implementation_notes: Frontend: implement virtualized table with sticky header and column pinning; perf budgets: 100ms initial render for 500 rows
Backend: normalized ledger endpoint must support query param 'pricing_preview=true' returning computed_cost and applied_pricing_pattern without final billing tags
Export: include manifest.json alongside parquet/CSV with schema version and pricing_metadata_ref
